subject: math
explanation: When multiplying powers with the same base, add the exponents: nᵃ × nᵇ = nᵃ⁺ᵇ. This works because nᵃ means a factors of n and nᵇ means b more factors — together there are a + b factors. Example: 2³ × 2⁴ = 2⁷ = 128. The law also holds for negative exponents: 10⁻² × 10⁻⁵ = 10⁻⁷. The base must be the same; you cannot combine 2³ × 3⁴ this way unless you compute values separately.

brainstorming.question: Why do we add exponents when bases match?
brainstorming.answer: Multiplying nᵃ × nᵇ joins a factors with b factors — total of a + b factors of n.

brainstorming.question: Can 2³ × 3² be simplified with one exponent?
brainstorming.answer: No — different bases. Evaluate 8 × 9 = 72 or leave as 2³ × 3².

brainstorming.question: Does the product law work for n⁰?

misconceptions.correct: Product law adds exponents; power-of-a-power multiplies them.

realLifeConnections.title: Combining bacterial generations
realLifeConnections.description: Doubling twice then three more times is 2² × 2³ = 2⁵ total doubling factor.

realLifeConnections.title: Stacking discounts
realLifeConnections.description: Two successive 10% reductions are not additive — but repeated scaling by powers models compounded effects.

realLifeConnections.title: Area scaling
realLifeConnections.description: Scaling a square side by 10² then 10³ multiplies area factor by 10⁵.

realLifeConnections.title: Memory addressing
realLifeConnections.description: Combining 2¹⁰ address lines with 2³ banks gives 2¹³ total addresses.

realLifeConnections.title: Chemistry concentrations
realLifeConnections.description: Diluting twice: multiply concentration factors using product of powers when same base ratio applies.

activities.title: Exponent addition strips
activities.instructions: Cut strips showing 2³ as three 2-blocks and 2⁴ as four 2-blocks. Join and count seven blocks → 2⁷.

activities.title: Same-base sort
activities.instructions: Sort cards into groups with matching bases. Simplify each group using the product law.

activities.title: Error hunt
activities.instructions: Find mistakes in expressions like 3⁴ × 3² = 3⁸ and 5⁻¹ × 5³ = 5⁻⁴. Correct and explain.

options: Cannot simplify with product law alone
